title: Polynomial Root Finder
description: Find all roots of a polynomial: exact quadratic formula for degree 2, Durand–Kerner iteration for higher degrees, with complex roots and verification.
howto: Type the coefficients from highest degree to constant, separated by spaces or commas (e.g. 1 -3 2).
Press Find Roots. Quadratics use the exact quadratic formula; degree 3+ uses the Durand–Kerner method.
Read every root — real and complex — with the iteration count.
Check the verification: each root plugged back into the polynomial ≈ 0.

faqs.a: An iterative root-finding algorithm that refines all roots simultaneously: each root estimate is updated by dividing the polynomial's value at that point by the product of differences to the other estimates, converging to all roots including complex ones.
Iteration stops when every root changes by less than 10⁻¹² between steps (max 500 iterations), and the tool verifies each root by evaluating the polynomial at it.

faqs.q: What coefficient order do I type?
faqs.a: Highest degree first: for x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6 type 1 -6 11 -6. The degree is the number of coefficients minus one (max 8).
